summary: Full end-to-end testing of STRATEX HABITAT MVP. Backend: 29/29 pytest tests passed covering auth, RBAC, properties, analytics (5 assets, 8 findings, 3 reports, 3 docs, 3 maintenance), quote create+respond flow, marketplace routing, contractor profile upsert, reviews with rating recompute, and STRATEX Core mock publish (5 assets published). Frontend: Login (3 roles), Digital Twin dashboard with Inspector (Roof — North Slope thermal finding, $2,450-$3,200, Insulation Upgrade), Top Contractor Quotes (Horizon $2,780 Best match, PeakBuild $2,950, Lonestar $3,210), Request Quote dialog → new quote appears in /quotes, Marketplace lead respond dialog, Contractor profile save, Contractor detail dual scorecard (Public 5.0 + STRATEX A+) with 5 scorecard bars and verified reviews, Add Review flow, Executive Core publish — all PASS.
action_items: OPTIONAL — Naming inconsistency: Respond dialog uses testids resp-low/resp-high/resp-scope/resp-timeline/resp-submit but the review_request implied respond-{id} pattern. Field testids work correctly via UI; consider renaming for consistency with respond-{id} trigger.
OPTIONAL — Executive demo login lands on /twin instead of /marketplace. core-publish-btn is present on /marketplace and works there. Consider redirecting executive to /marketplace on demo login.

OPTIONAL — Findings page renders 12 elements matching [data-testid^='finding-'] because nested children also share that prefix (finding-priority, finding-quote, etc). Use a more specific prefix like finding-row- for top-level items to make E2E selection unambiguous.
NOTE — A spurious 401 console error on initial /login page load comes from /api/auth/me probe; harmless.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 547 lines and contains all routes + storage helpers + seed wiring. Consider splitting into routers/ modules (auth.py, properties.py, quotes.py, contractors.py, core.py) once it grows beyond 700 lines.
set_auth_cookie uses secure=False — acceptable for preview, but for production behind HTTPS set secure=True (e.g. driven by an env flag).
core/publish blindly marks ALL assets across all properties as published; if multi-tenant scaling is planned, scope updates to a property_id or owner.
CORS allow_origins reads from env split by ',' but defaults to '*'; combined with allow_credentials=True this is a permissive default — fine for dev preview.
MongoDB _id is consistently excluded via projections — good.
Password hashing uses bcrypt with $2b$ format — verified via login flow (correct).

seed_data_creation: Backend tests created TEST_ prefixed quote ('TEST_ Quote Roof') and review ('TEST review' on first contractor). UI tests created an additional quote 'TEST_UI Quote E2E 2026'. All test data is non-destructive and clearly prefixed for cleanup if needed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 8 review-request scenarios verified end-to-end (auth, dashboard content, request quote flow, page listings, contractor respond, contractor profile save, reviews + dual scorecard, Core handshake + RBAC). pytest suite at /app/backend/tests/test_backend.py is the regression baseline. Note that POST /core/publish is idempotent and published_assets becomes 5 after first run — adjust if seeded count changes.
